personality_one_liner: A high-performance, command-center interface designed for deep focus and academic tracking, using sharp typography and a warm rust accent to communicate effort and progress.

spacing.rule: Use tight, utility-driven spacing. Ensure high visual density without feeling cramped by leaning on consistent 4px/8px baselines.

do's: Use solid surfaceSecondary and surfaceTertiary for elevation.
Use border separators for hierarchy instead of shadows or blur.
dont's: Do not use glass or blur effects; keep the interface sharp and operational.

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: A command-center dashboard showing today's study progress, daily goals, XP/level, and quick access to start studying.

states.empty: No data yet—prompt user to start their first study session.

screens.layout: Use a stacked card layout. Top section features a textured background with the user's Level and XP progress bar. Below that, a prominent circular progress ring for the daily goal (e.g., 2h / 4h studied). Follow with a 2-column grid for 'Current Streak' and 'Completed Tasks' metric cards. Pin a sticky 'Start Studying' CTA at the bottom using brandPrimary.

screens.name: Tasks
screens.purpose: Manage study tasks with due dates and subject tags, awarding XP upon completion.

states.empty: Illustration of a clean minimal desk workspace. 'No tasks due. Take a break or add a new task!'

screens.layout: List view. Each row uses surfaceSecondary with left-aligned checkboxes (circular). Include subject chips (brandTertiary tinted) and due dates (condensed text). Provide a floating action button (FAB) for adding tasks.

screens.name: Timer
screens.purpose: A focused, distraction-free Pomodoro timer interface.
screens.layout: Full-screen utility layout. Center a massive circular countdown timer using the Barlow Condensed display font (oversized, e.g., 64pt+). Below the timer, include segmented controls or pills for presets (25/5, 50/10, Custom). Above the timer, a dropdown/selector for the 'Subject'. Large, tactile Play/Pause buttons at the bottom.

screens.name: Statistics
screens.purpose: Visualize academic productivity through charts and gamification achievements.
screens.layout: Segmented into 'Metrics' and 'Achievements'. Metrics features a weekly bar chart (using react-native-gifted-charts with brandPrimary bars on surfaceSecondary) and a subject breakdown (pie chart or list). Achievements displays a grid of badges (tinted containers for unlocked, muted opacity for locked).

screens.name: Settings
screens.purpose: Manage app preferences, daily goals, and custom subjects.
screens.layout: Standard list layout with right-aligned chevrons or toggles. Group settings into 'Preferences' (Daily Goal, Notification), 'Subjects' (Manage list), and 'Data'. Use surfaceSecondary for list rows.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Dark-First Utility (Personality 7) rules. The interface must feel like a live operational surface, prioritizing scannability and contrast.
Do NOT use glassmorphism or blur effects. Use solid borders and tonal separation (surfaceSecondary, surfaceTertiary) to create hierarchy.
Use Barlow Condensed for large numbers (Timer countdown, XP, Level, Stat numbers) and Manrope for all general UI reading.
Ensure the Pomodoro Timer screen features a large, oversized circular progress indicator and massive numbers (minimum 64pt).
Implement gamification cleanly: XP bars and levels should feel like performance metrics, not childish toys. Avoid neon/cyberpunk styles; stick to the warm rust/amber accent.
For the Timer screen, the Subject Selector must be visually prominent before the timer starts.
When applying images (like the home header bg or empty state), use the mandatory vertical linear-gradient scrim (top-to-bottom transparent to surfaceInverse or surface) to ensure text readability.
Use react-native-gifted-charts for Statistics and ensure the chart styling matches the minimal dark theme (hide grid lines, use brandPrimary for bars).
Wire haptics to all key interactions as specified in the haptics block.
